category: game server control plane with a UDP traffic relay

free_tier.stated: One host - your own PC - is free with no time limit, for as many game servers as your hardware can run: the web panel and console, the config editor, the mod manager, auto-restart on crash and the traffic relay.

egress.terms: No byte allowance is published anywhere read: 'Your first BYOH node is completely free - no time limits, no credit card, all features included.'; ingress: tcp+udp

interface_detail: An agent binary plus a web panel; the pages read describe no public API and no tunnel-only command.
tooling: nodemesh agent (sudo install script on Linux), web panel, console; no standalone tunnel CLI is documented
chaining: The agent is the only thing that must run, so it fits a free Linux VM; the game server itself is installed by the platform.

limits.value: no byte allowance published for the traffic proxy

binding_note: Nothing published caps 1 TiB/month, so the volume test can be neither failed nor passed from documents. The named constraint is the one the vendor states instead of a quota: the relay is 'Not DDoS protection', and in relay mode 'The game sees every player as one local address, so IP bans don't work.'

identity_cost.detail: A signup with a verified email: 'Create a free account', and crash alerts go to 'your verified email'.

reliability_note: Relay mode collapses every player to one local address, so per-player IP bans stop working; the vendor says the relay is not DDoS protection; a node that goes offline pauses its servers and disconnects players.
confidence_note: Running the agent and pushing a counted volume through the proxy would show whether an unpublished cap or throttle exists, and a probe record would make this measured.

evidence.proved: 'Bedrock uses UDP on port 19132 (IPv4) and 19133 (IPv6). The relay forwards them to your PC, so you make no changes to your router.'
'TCP and UDP both supported' under Traffic Proxy, and 'Included free with your first BYOH node'
In relay mode: 'The game sees every player as one local address, so IP bans don't work.' and 'Not DDoS protection.'
'Your first BYOH node is completely free - no time limits, no credit card, all features included.' and 'This is free forever - not just during beta.'
Extra nodes 'cost 5 NMC/month each', so the free unit is one node rather than a byte count
The agent install is 'curl -sSL https://install.nodemesh.app | sudo sh', and the origin must be Linux: 'It needs a Linux host'

notes: Beta, stated on the page: 'you can create this server today, but we have not run it on our own hardware yet'. The free unit is one host, so a second machine needs credits. The relay is documented for game servers; the site does not offer a generic arbitrary-UDP port, so whether a non-game UDP listener works behind it is unstated.

extras.wg_detail: No WireGuard mode of its own; the relay is documented as carrying UDP, so a WireGuard datagram to the proxy address is the same path. Untested.
extras.volume_stated: No byte allowance is published anywhere read: 'Your first BYOH node is completely free - no time limits, no credit card, all features included.'
extras.transit_note: NodeMesh's edge proxy carries the player traffic; the origin only makes an outbound connection.
